item.research_question: What are the magnetic properties of the as-cast high-entropy alloy FeCoNiTi, specifically regarding the origin of its multiple ferromagnetic transitions and the mechanism behind the high coercive field observed in the fcc phase?
item.material_system: FeCoNiTi (equiatomic Fe:Co:Ni:Ti = 1:1:1:1) and a C14-dominant variant Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29
item.processing_route: Arc melting of elemental chips/wires (99.9% purity) in an Ar atmosphere on a water-cooled Cu hearth followed by rapid quenching to produce as-cast polycrystalline samples
item.test_conditions: DC magnetization measured from 50 to 1150 K under 100 Oe; Isothermal magnetization curves at 50, 100, 200, 300, and 400 K; Electronic structure calculations using CPA with PBE potential
key_findings: The alloy exhibits three distinct ferromagnetic transitions at 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
The fcc phase is responsible for the high-temperature ordering at 1084 K and the low-temperature ordering at 168 K.
The hexagonal C14 Laves phase is responsible for the ferromagnetic ordering at 214 K.
The coercive field (Hc) of the fcc phase reaches 667 Oe at 400 K and 489 Oe at 300 K.
Electronic structure calculations confirm ferromagnetic ground states for both fcc and C14 phases.
Theoretical saturation magnetization (Ms) for the fcc phase is 78.6 emu/g, while the experimental value at 50 K is 43 emu/g.
Ti atoms exhibit antiferromagnetic coupling with Fe, Co, and Ni atoms in both phases.
A negative correlation exists between Hc and Ms in fcc HEAs based on FeCoNi, suggesting magnetocrystalline anisotropy governs Hc.
item.mechanism: The high coercive field in the fcc phase is not primarily driven by orbital moments but is partially attributed to magnetocrystalline anisotropy, which follows an inverse relationship with saturation magnetization (Hc ∝ 1/Ms). The presence of Ti induces antiferromagnetic coupling that reduces Ms, thereby enhancing Hc.
item.limitations: Theoretical Ms values consistently surpass experimental counterparts, indicating the presence of a spin-canted component in the actual magnetic structure not captured by the parallel spin model.
item.future_work: The discussion provides a strategic avenue for manipulating fundamental magnetic properties by deliberately reducing Ms to augment Hc in fcc magnetic HEAs based on FeCoNi.
quotes: The HEA manifests three distinct ferromagnetic orderings at 1084, 214, and 168 K.
The coercive field of the fcc phase attains 667 Oe at 400 K.
